convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom to load two custom indicators (CCIT3_Simple_v_2-01 and CCIT3_noReCalc_v_3-01) for signal generation. The T3 smoothing logic inside these custom indicators must be reimplemented in Python since there is no built-in MT5 T3-CCI indicator.

derived_values.name: T3 smoothing coefficients
derived_values.formula: b2=Koeff_B^2, b3=b2*Koeff_B, c1=-b3, c2=3*(b2+b3), c3=-3*(2*b2+Koeff_B+b3), c4=1+3*Koeff_B+b3+3*b2

other_exits: When Trade_overturn=true: closes current position and opens opposite on CCIT3 zero-line crossover; SL/TP modification retried up to N_modify_sltp times with 1s delay between attempts

position_sizing.conditional_logic: If Max_drawdown<=0, use fixed Lots. If Max_drawdown>0, compute size=NormalizeDouble(Lots*AccountBalance/Max_drawdown, 2), capped at SYMBOL_VOLUME_MAX.

custom_logic_notes: The EA uses two variants of a custom CCIT3 indicator (Simple vs noReCalc), selectable via input flags but mutually exclusive. The noReCalc variant recalculates from bar 0 each tick (forward loop i=0..start), while the Simple variant processes from oldest to newest (reverse loop i=start..0). The T3 smoothing is a 6-stage EMA cascade applied to raw CCI values; values above 1000 are clamped to 0. The CCIT3 crossover uses bars [0] and [1] (CopyBuffer offset 1, count 2). Trailing stop only activates when position is profitable and updates Trail_stop variable to prevent backward movement. SL/TP are set after position open via separate TRADE_ACTION_SLTP request with retry logic (N_modify_sltp attempts).
python_conversion_notes: Must reimplement the full T3-CCI calculation in Python: (1) compute raw CCI using standard formula, (2) apply 6-stage EMA cascade with T3 coefficients, (3) compute final output as c1*e6+c2*e5+c3*e4+c4*e3. Key difference between Simple and noReCalc: Simple iterates from oldest-to-newest (preserving EMA state across bars naturally), noReCalc resets e1-e6 to 0 at each bar (forward loop from i=0). The crossover signal checks CCIT3[0]<=0 && CCIT3[1]>0 (bearish crossover = sell) and CCIT3[0]>=0 && CCIT3[1]<0 (bullish crossover = buy). Note the entry logic uses CopyBuffer with shift=1 so bars [0] and [1] refer to the previous completed bar and the one before it — this is a 'confirmed bar' check, not a current-bar repaint. SL/TP are in points (not pips), and the 1750 TP with default 0 SL suggests a wide target. The trailing stop uses Point() directly so no digit adjustment is needed. The SL/TP modify-after-open pattern must be replicated or replaced with order-level SL/TP in Python.
